content:
ops-bot: INCIDENT alert — p95 latency spike in eu-west1 (SLO breach). Details: https://alerts.redwood.local/incident/INC-2026-3467 :exclamation: Affected service: inference-runtime (streaming + generation). Auto-detect: p95=345ms (target 200ms), p99=1.2s. Starting triage.

maya: ack, i'm oncall — collecting baseline dashboards now. tagging @leo for on-call SRE handoff if needed.

sam: metrics snapshot: p95 345ms, p99 1.2s, streaming stalls increased x8 in last 10m. KV cache eviction rate spiked from 120/s -> 980/s. Prefill queue length > 4000. top affected model: "redwood/rlhf-12b-v2" on shard-12.

maya: log tail from runtime (cut):
```
[2026-03-15T16:04:12Z] kv_cache: eviction shard=12 rate=980/s free=1.2GB
[2026-03-15T16:04:22Z] prefill: enqueue 342 items (decode backlog)
[2026-03-15T16:04:30Z] streaming: stall detected session=abc123 wait=1050ms
```

leo: noted. initial hypothesis: cache fragmentation + prefill vs decode imbalance — prefill workers racing to allocate slabs causing decode starvation -> tail latencies and streaming stalls. Could also be exacerbated by recent model rollout with bigger KV sizes.

maya: can we temporarily lower prefill concurrency or throttle prefill per-shard? I want to avoid full reroute unless necessary.

sam: tried a quick PromQL to confirm per-shard prefill vs decode ratio:
```
(sum(rate(prefill.requests[1m])) by (shard) / sum(rate(decode.requests[1m])) by (shard)) > 4
```
shard-12 ratio=7.1, others ~1.1.

leo: mitigation options: 1) reduce prefill concurrency 2) bump slab allocation threshold on shard-12 3) enable immediate eviction backpressure to slow prefill 4) route traffic off shard-12 to cold fallback pool.

maya: i'll try (1) first. applying runtime flag: `runtimectl set prefill.concurrency=2 --shard=12`

infra-bot: runtimectl change queued by maya. Plan:apply in 10s.

deploy-bot: change applied to shard-12: prefill.concurrency=2 — rollout ok (3 nodes): https://deploys.redwood.local/changes/8743

sam: after change p95 dropped to 210ms in 60s, p99 to 520ms, streaming stalls down ~60%. eviction rate fell to 240/s.

leo: good signal. still seeing some p99 spikes correlated with decode GC around 2026-03-15T16:06:xx — might need slab tuning.

maya: customer-impact check: @customer-support can you list customers affected in last 30m? priority customers only.

customer-support: quick list: AcmePayments (EU), Finscale (EU) had elevated latencies; 2 support tickets opened, no data loss. Escalated to enterprise leads. Customer Slack pings sent.

maya: handing off to @leo for continuity. i'll continue observation for 30m then sign off if stable. ETA 16:45Z.

leo: taking over. next steps: schedule slab compaction on shard-12 + increase min_slab_size by 25% if we see fragmentation persist. Also will consider gradual model-variant fallback if p95 doesn't stabilize.

ops-bot: INCIDENT update — mitigation reduced customer impact. Current state: mitigated (partial). Incident will remain open for postmortem. #s: p95=198ms, p99=460ms, streaming stalls baseline restored.

maya: adding notes for postmortem: root cause suspected = KV cache fragmentation + prefill/decode imbalance after recent model rollout increased kv-entry size. Follow-ups: a) add per-shard prefill backpressure metric + alert b) run offline slab-defrag for shard-12 c) test prefill rate-limiter in staging.

sam: captured graphs: https://metrics.redwood.local/d/incident-3467

leo: ack. handing off to oncall-next (erin) at 16:50Z — ping me if it flares.

erin: noted, i'll watch until 17:30Z. keep me posted, thanks :thumbsup: 

customer-support: posted proactive message to AcmePayments + Finscale: "We're investigating intermittent latency spikes in EU; we've applied mitigations; monitoring. Will follow up with timeline and postmortem." They appreciated proactive notice.

maya: thanks team. tagging #postmortem when ready. closing thread for realtime updates.
